interest: Full roster of the Kempeitai in northern Indochina at Japan's surrender.
overview: This file contains a May 22, 1946 memorandum from the War Department's Strategic Services Unit (SSU) transmitting an intelligence report to the Department of State regarding Japanese intelligence and military police (Kempeitai) personnel in French Indochina. The enclosed report, current as of September 1, 1945, provides a comprehensive personnel roster of the Japanese Military Police of the Southern Area Command operating north of the 16th parallel. It details the leadership and headquarters sections in Hanoi—including wireless transmission, secret police, police affairs, and general administration—as well as regional gendarmerie detachments in Langson, Vinh, Lao Cai, Vinh Yen, Luang Prabang, Pakse, Hue, Haiphong, Lai Chau, and Son La. The document systematically records individual ranks, duties, and original army branch attachments, capturing the complete Kempeitai apparatus in northern Indochina at the conclusion of the Second World War.

subfiles.about: Comprehensive roster and organizational listing of Japanese Military Police (Kempeitai) officers and personnel in northern French Indochina as of September 1, 1945.
subfiles.summary: An intelligence summary providing a detailed nominal roster of the officers, non-commissioned officers, and enlisted men of the Japanese Military Police (Kempeitai) of the Southern Area Command north of Latitude 16 degrees in French Indochina, current as of September 1, 1945. It delineates the central headquarters in Hanoi across wireless, secret police, police affairs, and general affairs sections, noting personnel seconded from regular army units such as infantry, artillery, and engineers. It further details individual postings for regional gendarmerie detachments in Langson, Vinh, Lao Cai, Vinh Yen, Luang Prabang, Pakse, Hue, Haiphong, Lai Chau, and Son La.
subfiles.title: Roster of Japanese Military Police (Kempeitai) Personnel in French Indo-China
